chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: What set the Hines band apart: arrangements

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Were there other big bands around Chicago then? That, you know, didn't get as well known as Earl, but good bands?
Big bands, I think we was the only big band in Chicago.

How do you see the basic difference between the Earl Hines Band in Chicago and the other big bands that were popular during that time? What was the special difference, besides, you know, the soloists?
The arrangements.
The arrangements?
Mostly the other bands had stock
arrangements.
Jimmy Mundy continued to write for the band after he left, didn't he?
Yeah, he did a little writing after he left.
Did the Hines Band use any stock arrangements, of, say --
Yeah --
(Inaudible).
Yeah, we used stocks.
Did you doctor them?
A few of them we'd doctor up. Not too many. We'd just play them like, you know -- most of the time we played stocks when Earl was off the stand.
Did Earl read well?
Yeah. Oh, yeah, he could read.
Did he play the shows?
Uh-huh. Played and conducted the shows.
(Recording interruption.)
